messages:
alex: quick sync — we need to decide on 'trust zones' across hosted/dedicated/private. who owns identity translation and when routing can fallback across zones? :thinking:
maria: +1. recent incident showed private sidecar losing control-plane access and traffic silently fell back to hosted. we need explicit rules not implicit behavior. :eyes:
jordan: can you sketch the constraint matrix? latency/SLO, data residency, auth boundary.
samir: rough idea: three zones — 1) control-plane (CP) trust, 2) runtime-only (RT) trust, 3) cross-zone fallback (F). each zone has allowed actions: token-exchange, KV cache access, model routing.
anya: important: private mode must never cross PII/policy boundaries without explicit opt-in. fallback should be opt-in per-tenant and logged.
alex: agree. tradeoffs: if we forbid fallback for private tenants, SLA/availability drops. if we allow it, we risk data egress. propose a policy enum: {no-fallback, metrics-only-fallback, full-fallback} per-tenant + a default for SaaS customers.
maria: +1 on enum. also need a simple wire for audit: when fallback occurs, emit structured event with fields: tenant_id, reason, dst_zone, model_variant.
samir: implementation note: token propagation differs per zone. we can do signed short-lived mTLS certs for RT zone, and opaque bearer for hosted. translation should be a simple adapter: `translate_token(src, dst_zone)` with policy table.
jordan: what about billing attribution when fallback happens? Hosted should bill, but dedicated reserved capacity shouldn't be charged incorrectly. need attribution headers.
anya: header approach fine, but dedicated/private ops will require ability to reject requests lacking header provenance. so adapters must add `X-RW-Provenance: zone=rt;adapter=sidecar;orig=private` and sign it.
alex: config snippet proposal (pseudofile):
```
fallback_policy:
  tenant_overrides:
    tenant-123: no-fallback
  default: metrics-only-fallback
audit_sink: controlplane.elsa
provenance_header: X-RW-Provenance
```
any concerns?
maria: how to handle offline private (air-gapped) where control-plane is unreachable? metrics-only-fallback makes no sense — we need local-only fallbacks like warm model cache. maybe add `local-grace-mode` that serves cached model slices.
samir: agree — add `grace_modes: [local-cache, retry-without-telemetry]` and require tenant opt-in. also ensure KMS keys never leave the private network.
jordan: operationally, we need probes to validate policy enforcement. small probe matrix: verify token-translation rejects, provenance header presence/validity, fallback audit emitted.
anya: can we centralize policy in CP? CP expresses allowed transitions; adapters fetch a signed policy blob and enforce locally. this reduces latencies of policy checks.
alex: action items: 1) PR for enum + config schema (samir), 2) telemetry event shape + sink (maria), 3) adapter provenance header spec + signing (jordan), 4) air-gap grace-mode design doc (anya). I'll create tickets.
maria: adding: add tests for billing attribution and a canary that forces fallback to hosted to verify billing headers.
deploy-bot: [deploy] policy-service v2.3 rolled to staging (cd-789) — smoke tests queued. :rocket:
anya: thanks — can we gate rollout behind a feature-flag per-tenant? safer.
alex: yes. feature-flag + staged rollout. ok wrapping up — I'll file a followup RFC with diagrams and the probe matrix.
maria: thanks all.
